# Icon

A Lucide glyph sized from the size.icon.* scale, inheriting its colour from the text around it.

```tsx
import { Icon } from "@rata/icons";
```

### `icon`

```ts
icon: LucideIcon
```

The Lucide component to render, passed as a value rather than a name.

Source doc: The Lucide component to render, passed as a value so the set stays tree-shakeable.

**Use when**

- Any icon imported from `@rata/icons` — the curated set — or from `lucide-react` directly when the set is missing one.
- Passing the component itself (`icon={Trash2}`), which is what keeps the icon set tree-shakeable: a string name would force every icon into the bundle.

**Don't use for**

- Rendering the Lucide component directly instead of through `Icon`. It would take Lucide's default 24px rather than a step from the scale, and it would not get the a11y switch below.
- An emoji or a text glyph as a stand-in. Those inherit font metrics rather than the icon scale, so they will not line up with real icons beside them.

**Accessibility** Rendered `aria-hidden` unless `label` is set — see `label`.

### `size`

```ts
size?: IconSize = "text"
```

Which step of the `size.icon.*` scale the glyph is drawn at. Defaults to following the surrounding text.

Source doc: Which step of the `size.icon.*` scale to draw at. Defaults to following the surrounding text.

**Use when**

- Leave it alone for anything with text near it — the default `text` step is 1.15em, so the glyph tracks whatever font-size it lands in and needs no decision per control.
- `xs` / `sm` / `md` / `lg` only for a standalone glyph with no text to inherit from: a status dot in a table cell, or an icon-only control whose name is an `aria-label` rather than visible text.
- `lg` when the glyph should render unscaled — 24px is Lucide's native artboard.

**Don't use for**

- Picking a fixed step to match a control's size. A control's `size` changes its box, not its text, so an icon inside it should not change either — and a fixed step stops matching the moment the surrounding text does change.
- Mixing steps within one row of icons — they read as a set, so they measure as a set.

### `label`

```ts
label?: string
```

Accessible name, for an icon that carries meaning nothing else conveys.

**Use when**

- An icon that is the only thing communicating something — a status glyph in a table cell with no adjacent text.

**Don't use for**

- An icon inside a `Button` with `iconOnly`. That button already carries the `aria-label` the contract requires, so labelling the icon too announces the same thing twice.
- An icon sitting beside a visible text label. The text is the name; the icon is decoration and must stay hidden from assistive technology.

**Accessibility** Present, the glyph becomes `role="img"` with this as its name. Absent, it is `aria-hidden` — the same switch `Spinner` uses for the same reason, and the reason the decorative case needs no thought to get right.

### `className`

```ts
className?: string
```

Extra classes on the glyph, for placement — not for restyling it.

**Use when**

- A layout concern the parent cannot express, such as a margin token when the icon is not already inside a flex row with a gap.

**Don't use for**

- Overriding the size. The four steps are the scale; a fifth size written in a component's CSS is the drift `size.icon.*` exists to prevent — add a step to the scale instead.
- Setting a colour. The glyph strokes with `currentColor` so it always matches the text it sits in; colouring it separately is how an icon ends up contradicting its own label.

## Use cases

### Inside an icon-only button

The most common pairing, and the one where the a11y split matters most.

```tsx
<Button iconOnly aria-label="Delete row">
  <Icon icon={Trash2} />
</Button>
```

No `label` on the icon: the button owns the accessible name, so the glyph stays `aria-hidden`. `size` is left at `md`, which is what a 32px control wants.

### Beside a text label

An action whose icon reinforces a word rather than replacing it.

```tsx
<Button>
  <Icon icon={Download} />
  Export CSV
</Button>
```

No `size`: the default `text` step is 1.15em, so the glyph is sized from the button's own label and stays matched to it. The icon is decorative here, so it takes no `label` either.

### Carrying meaning on its own

A status glyph in a dense row, with no adjacent text to name it.

```tsx
<Icon icon={CircleAlert} size="xs" label="Needs review" />
```

This is the only case that takes a `label`. Without one the row would announce nothing at all where a sighted user sees a warning.

## Real usage in this repo

```tsx
<Icon icon={User} />
```

## Token recipe

### base

A glyph sized from the text around it, taking its colour from that text too.

| Property | Token |
|---|---|
| width | `size.icon.text — 1.15em, so it follows the inherited font-size. size.icon.xs / .sm / .md / .lg for a standalone glyph.` |
| height | `same step as width; the scale is one number and the glyph is square` |
| stroke | `currentColor — the icon inherits the colour of the text it sits in, so it needs no colour token of its own and cannot contradict its label` |
| flex-shrink | `0 — a glyph beside text must not be squeezed by it, which is a layout fact rather than a token` |
